title: Cell Processes and Organization
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Cell Processes and Organization Worksheets (Ontario Curriculum)
standard_text: Explain diffusion and osmosis across the cell membrane; describe specialized cells and how cells form tissues, organs and organ systems; assess how cell research has contributed to health and medicine. (summary of the Ontario Science and Technology curriculum, 2022, Strand B: Life Systems – Cells)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 science worksheets on diffusion, osmosis, specialized cells, tissues and organs, and cells and health. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Particles move from high to low concentration.
key_sub: Osmosis moves water across membranes; specialized cells form tissues, organs and systems.
body_html:
How to think about it

Diffusion: particles move from where there are many to where there are few.

  • Osmosis: water diffuses across a selectively permeable membrane.
  • Specialized cells have shapes that fit their jobs (nerve, red blood, root hair cells).
  • Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism.
Example

A potato slice is put in salty water. What happens?

water moves to the saltier side

Answer: it loses water and goes limp

Example

Why do root hair cells have long extensions?

more surface area

Answer: to absorb more water

Common mistakes

  • Thinking osmosis moves salt instead of water.
  • Thinking all cells look the same.
  • Thinking diffusion needs energy from the cell.

faq.q: What is the difference between diffusion and osmosis?
faq.a: Diffusion is the movement of any particles from high to low concentration. Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a membrane.
A cell with a special shape or parts for its job, like a long nerve cell or a red blood cell with no nucleus.
It has led to vaccines, cancer treatments and stem-cell therapies. Stem cells were discovered by Canadian scientists in Toronto.

items.q: What is diffusion?
c: the making of food by plants
movement from low to high concentration only
the movement of particles from an area of high concentration to an area of low concentration
items.e: Oxygen diffuses into cells.

items.q: Oxygen moves from the air sacs in the lungs into the blood. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: What is osmosis?
c: the movement of food in the stomach
the diffusion of water across a cell membrane
items.e: Water moves toward the side with more dissolved substances.

items.q: Digested food enters the blood. Where does this mainly happen?
c: the air sacs of the lungs
the villi of the small intestine
items.e: Exchange surfaces are large and thin for fast diffusion.

items.q: Which is a way that cells help keep the body healthy?
items.e: White blood cells are part of the immune system.

items.q: Water moves from cell to cell across a root towards the xylem. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: A cube has sides of 3 cm. What is its surface area?
A slice of potato is placed in very salty water. What happens?
c: Water leaves the potato cells by osmosis, so the slice becomes soft and limp.
The potato gains water and swells.
items.e: Water moves to the saltier side.

items.q: Mineral salts move into root hair cells from a higher concentration in the soil. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: Why do wilted celery sticks become firm in fresh water?
c: Water enters the cells by osmosis and fills the vacuoles.
The celery grows new cells in minutes.
items.e: Turgor keeps plants firm.

items.q: Carbon dioxide moves from body cells into the blood. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: Oxygen moves from the blood in capillaries into body cells. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: How has cell research helped medicine?
c: Understanding cells led to vaccines, cancer treatments and stem-cell research.
It has not helped at all.
items.e: Canadian researchers discovered stem cells in 1961.

items.q: A cube has sides of 4 cm. What is its surface area to volume ratio?
items.e: 96 ÷ 64 = 1.5. Larger organisms have a smaller ratio, so they need a transport system.

items.q: A cube has sides of 2 cm. What is its volume?
Oxygen and glucose pass from the blood to muscle cells. Where does this mainly happen?
c: the air sacs of the lungs
items.e: Exchange surfaces are large and thin for fast diffusion.

items.q: Why do root hair cells have long thin extensions?
c: to protect the root from insects
to increase surface area for taking in water
items.e: More surface area means more absorption.

items.q: Oxygen enters the blood. Where does this mainly happen?
c: the villi of the small intestine
the air sacs of the lungs
items.e: Exchange surfaces are large and thin for fast diffusion.

items.q: Carbon dioxide enters a leaf through the stomata. Which process is this?
items.e: Diffusion: net movement of particles from a higher to a lower concentration. Osmosis: water moving through a partially permeable membrane.

items.q: Carbon dioxide enters a leaf. Where does this mainly happen?
c: the villi of the small intestine
items.e: Exchange surfaces are large and thin for fast diffusion.

items.q: Which specialized cell is long with branches to carry electrical messages?
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Which specialized cell has lots of mitochondria and can contract?
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: How is an egg cell adapted for its job?
c: It has tiny hairs that sweep mucus out of the airways.
It is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
It has no nucleus and a dimpled shape to carry lots of oxygen.
It is large and contains a food store for the growing embryo.
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Cell A has 13 units of carbon dioxide and cell B has 21 units. Which way will carbon dioxide diffuse?
c: from cell A to cell B
from cell B to cell A
it will move both ways equally for ever
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: How is a sperm cell adapted for its job?
c: It has a tail to swim to the egg.
It is large and contains a food store for the growing embryo.
It has lots of mitochondria and can contract.
It is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis.
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Where is the chloroplast found?
c: in both plant and animal cells
items.e: Only plant cells in the green parts, such as leaf cells, have chloroplasts.

items.q: How is a nerve cell adapted for its job?
c: It has a long, thin hair to take in water from the soil.
It has a tail to swim to the egg.
It has lots of mitochondria and can contract.
It is long with branches to carry electrical messages.
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Where is the cytoplasm found?
c: in both plant and animal cells
items.e: Both plant and animal cells have a cytoplasm.

items.q: Which specialized cell is packed with chloroplasts for photosynthesis?
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Why are nerve cells long?
c: to carry messages over long distances in the body
items.e: Specialized cells have special shapes.

items.q: By diffusion, which way does carbon dioxide move here: from the blood or into the air in the lungs?
c: from the air in the lungs into the blood
from the blood into the air in the lungs
it does not move at all
items.e: Particles diffuse from where there are a lot of them (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).

items.q: Where is the cell membrane found?
c: in both plant and animal cells
items.e: Both plant and animal cells have a cell membrane.

items.q: Which specialized cell has a tail to swim to the egg?
items.e: Specialized cells have features that suit their jobs.

items.q: Where is the nucleus found?
c: in both plant and animal cells
items.e: Both plant and animal cells have a nucleus.

items.q: Cell A has 26 units of oxygen and cell B has 28 units. Which way will oxygen diffuse?
c: from cell B to cell A
from cell A to cell B
it will move both ways equally for ever
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: Cell A has 28 units of carbon dioxide and cell B has 17 units. Which way will carbon dioxide diffuse?
c: from cell A to cell B
from cell B to cell A
it will move both ways equally for ever
items.e: Diffusion goes from high to low concentration.

items.q: Why do cells divide?
c: for growth, repair and to replace old cells
items.e: Skin cells are replaced every few weeks.

items.q: Why does a red blood cell have no nucleus?
c: There is more space to carry oxygen.
items.e: Its form suits its function.

items.q: By diffusion, which way does oxygen move here: from inside a leaf or out into the air in sunlight?
c: out from the air in sunlight into inside a leaf
it does not move at all
from inside a leaf out into the air in sunlight
items.e: Particles diffuse from where there are a lot of them (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).

items.q: What does 'selectively permeable' mean?
c: lets some substances through but not others
items.e: The cell membrane is selectively permeable.

items.q: Is the heart a cell, a tissue, an organ, an organ system or an organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: What is a tissue?
c: a group of similar cells working together
items.e: Muscle tissue.

items.q: What is the job of the nucleus?
c: It is a jelly where most chemical reactions happen.
It strengthens and supports the cell.
It is filled with cell sap and keeps the cell firm.
It controls the cell and contains the genetic material (DNA).
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Is a red blood cell a cell, a tissue, an organ, an organ system or an organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: Which part of a cell controls the cell and contains the genetic material (DNA)?
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Why are some cells called specialized?
c: They have special features for a particular job.
They have no nucleus at all.
items.e: Shape fits job.

items.q: Which part of a cell is where respiration releases energy?
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Which part of a cell strengthens and supports the cell?
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: What is diffusion?
c: particles moving from low to high concentration
the spreading out of particles from high to low concentration
items.e: Smells spreading.

items.q: What is the job of the cell membrane?
c: It controls what enters and leaves the cell.
It is filled with cell sap and keeps the cell firm.
They are where respiration releases energy.
They are where photosynthesis makes food.
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: What is the job of the cytoplasm?
c: They are where respiration releases energy.
It strengthens and supports the cell.
It is a jelly where most chemical reactions happen.
They are where photosynthesis makes food.
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Is an oak tree a cell, a tissue, an organ, an organ system or an organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: Which organ system includes the heart and blood vessels?
items.e: It moves blood.

items.q: Is fat tissue a cell, a tissue, an organ, an organ system or an organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: Which level of organization comes just before organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: Which organ system breaks down food?
items.e: Mouth to intestines.

items.q: Is a muscle cell a cell, a tissue, an organ, an organ system or an organism?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: Which part of a cell controls what enters and leaves the cell?
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Which level of organization comes after organ?
items.e: Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organisms.

items.q: What is the job of the chloroplasts?
c: It controls what enters and leaves the cell.
They are where photosynthesis makes food.
It strengthens and supports the cell.
They are where respiration releases energy.
items.e: Each part of a cell has a job.

items.q: Each cell is 0.1 mm wide. How many cells would fit in a row 2 mm long?
Sofia looks at pond water under a microscope. Which organism is made of only one cell?
items.e: Unicellular organisms, like bacteria, amoebas and yeast, are made of a single cell.

items.q: A row of 10 identical cells measures 1 mm. How wide is one cell?
Why do leaf cells have many chloroplasts?
c: to trap light energy to make food
items.e: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll.

items.q: A cell has no cell wall and no chloroplasts. What could it be?
items.e: Animal cells have neither.

items.q: Emma makes a list of organisms. Which one is multicellular?
items.e: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

items.q: A row of 40 identical cells measures 1 mm. How wide is one cell?
A row of 25 identical cells measures 1 mm. How wide is one cell?
Noah looks at pond water under a microscope. Which organism is made of only one cell?
items.e: Unicellular organisms, like bacteria, amoebas and yeast, are made of a single cell.

items.q: What would happen to a cell with a damaged nucleus?
c: It would grow a cell wall.
It could not control its activities properly.
items.e: The nucleus controls the cell.

items.q: Which part do plant cells have that animal cells never have?
items.e: Some plant cells also have chloroplasts.

items.q: Benjamin makes a list of organisms. Which one is multicellular?
items.e: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

items.q: Each cell is 0.1 mm wide. How many cells would fit in a row 1 mm long?
Which living thing is made of only one cell?
items.e: Some living things, such as some bacteria and amoebae, are single cells.

items.q: Which part of a plant cell supports it so that the plant can stand upright?
items.e: Rigid cell walls help to support the plant.

items.q: Ava makes a list of organisms. Which one is multicellular?
items.e: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells, often of different types.

items.q: A cell has a cell wall but no chloroplasts. What could it be?
items.e: Onion skin cells do not get light, so they have no chloroplasts.

items.q: Each cell is 0.02 mm wide. How many cells would fit in a row 1 mm long?
Which instrument do we use to see cells?
items.e: Most cells are too small to see with our eyes.

items.q: Each cell is 0.02 mm wide. How many cells would fit in a row 5 mm long?
Cell X has a nucleus, a cell membrane, cytoplasm and a cell wall. Cell Y has a nucleus, a cell membrane and cytoplasm only. Which statement is correct?
c: X is a plant cell and Y is an animal cell.
X is an animal cell and Y is a plant cell.
items.e: Only plant cells have a cell wall.

items.q: Ava looked at cells from a green leaf and from an onion under a microscope. Which part did she see only in the leaf cells?
items.e: Both are plant cells; only the leaf cells have chloroplasts.

items.q: A red blood cell has no nucleus. What is the advantage?
c: There is more room to carry oxygen.
items.e: Adaptation.

items.q: Which blood vessel carries blood through the tissues, where substances are exchanged with the cells?
items.e: A capillary carries blood through the tissues, where substances are exchanged with the cells.

items.q: A student puts a balsam plant in red-coloured water. After a day, she cuts across the stem. Where is the red colour?
items.e: Xylem carries water up the stem.

items.q: Which blood vessel has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards?
items.e: A vein has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.

items.q: Why do plants wilt if their roots are damaged?
c: The leaves make too much food.
The phloem carries too much water.
Less water can be absorbed and carried up the xylem.
items.e: Water keeps cells firm.

items.q: Why does diffusion happen faster when it is warmer?
items.e: Temperature affects diffusion.

items.q: Why are farmers told not to over-fertilize? Too much fertilizer in the soil can
c: make the soil water more concentrated than the cell sap, so water leaves the roots by osmosis
items.e: The plants may wilt.

items.q: Why does euglena have both a chloroplast and an eyespot?
c: It is a plant cell only.
It can make food in light and swims towards light.
items.e: A unicellular organism.

items.q: Which describes an artery?
c: It has a wall only one cell thick.
It has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.
It has no wall at all.
It has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.
items.e: An artery has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.

items.q: Which describes a vein?
c: It has a wall only one cell thick.
It has a thick, muscular, elastic wall to withstand high pressure.
It has no wall at all.
It has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.
items.e: A vein has a thinner wall and valves to stop blood flowing backwards.

items.q: What is an amoeba?
c: a unicellular organism that moves and feeds by changing shape
items.e: One cell does everything.

items.q: Why do the lungs have a huge surface area?
c: so lots of oxygen can diffuse into the blood quickly
items.e: Bigger surface, faster diffusion.

items.q: Why does the blood in an artery spurt out when it is cut, but blood in a vein flows out slowly?
c: Blood in arteries is under much higher pressure.
items.e: Arteries carry blood pumped by the heart.

items.q: An amoeba is a single cell. Why does it not need a transport system?
c: It has a large surface area to volume ratio, so diffusion is fast enough.
items.e: Substances only need to travel a short distance.

items.q: What does an artery do?
c: It carries blood back to the heart.
It carries blood away from the heart.
It carries blood through the tissues, where substances are exchanged with the cells.
items.e: An artery carries blood away from the heart.

items.q: A pupil drew a cheek cell with a cell wall. What mistake did she make?
c: Animal cells do not have a cell wall.
Cheek cells have no cell membrane.
items.e: Only plant cells have a cell wall.

items.q: Jayden looked at cheek cells and onion cells. Which part did he see only in the onion cells?
items.e: Cheek cells are animal cells.

items.q: A person's capillaries are damaged. Which process is most affected?
c: the exchange of oxygen and food with body cells
items.e: Exchange happens across capillary walls.
